states.MATCH: The same qualified public form exists bilaterally and all declared language observables coincide.
states.ABSENT: The vanila qualified public form is valid, its controls pass, the crystalline product rejects that exact path specifically as absent, and no required independent probe demonstrates a related functional bilateral alternative. A skipped, unreachable, failed, or Unknown alternative probe can never establish ABSENT.
states.PARTIAL: The exact crystalline qualified form or a mandatory subset is unavailable, while a separately executed related alternative is valid, functional, and bilaterally demonstrated. This evidence takes PARTIAL over ABSENT and never upgrades the route to MATCH.
states.DIFFERENCE: Both products execute the same valid public form but differ in semantics, syntax, morphology, or exact public diagnostic.
states.UNKNOWN: Identity, construction, observer, parser/target/feature/fixture control, execution, resources, or evidence cannot support a decision. The reason must name the failing phase; an unsupported CLI option cannot be mislabeled as an expression-parser or route failure.
states.SCOPE_OUT: A currently valid ADR or exact Prompt L0 clause explicitly excludes the obligation; a name resemblance or current absence is insufficient.

decision_procedure: If an identity, mandatory control, qualified probe, required alternative probe, or required independent construction is unresolved, classify UNKNOWN.
Otherwise, if a current ADR or exact L0 clause explicitly excludes the obligation, classify SCOPE_OUT.
Otherwise, if the exact qualified form executes bilaterally, classify MATCH when all declared observables coincide and DIFFERENCE when any declared observable differs.

Otherwise, when the vanila qualified form is valid and the crystalline qualified form is specifically absent, classify PARTIAL if a required independent alternative probe demonstrates a related functional bilateral alternative.
Only otherwise classify ABSENT, after every applicable independent alternative probe completed conclusively without demonstrating a functional alternative.
classification_contract.precedence_note: PARTIAL and ABSENT are mutually exclusive. A demonstrated bilateral functional alternative requires PARTIAL; inconclusive alternative evidence requires UNKNOWN; ABSENT is the conclusive residual only after applicable alternatives are independently exercised.

math: qualified access in its own probe/process
bare or math-mode equivalent in a separate probe/process when it exists
the alternative probe must remain reachable after qualified access aborts
bare success requires PARTIAL when qualified access is absent and never establishes MATCH
html: HTML target selected symmetrically through compile --features html --format html
typst eval --target is forbidden in bilateral controls and route probes
independent parser/feature, target/fixture, and HTML API controls
separate missing tag/function from invalid args, prohibited content, target, or fixture failure
one independent html.elem literal-tag probe for every investigated html route
no generic div control can grant route-specific credit
color: do not substitute luma or color serialization
elements_introspection_helpers: construct a valid public instance in a probe independent from member access
do not construct through the qualified ancestor route under investigation
for nested members such as outline.entry.body, obtain the instance through an independent valid document/query/introspection route
run construction and member access separately when either can abort
use document projection when eval cannot observe the member
construction failure or ancestor-constructor absence is UNKNOWN, never ABSENT

alternative_probe_contract.receipt_independence: Each qualified, alternative, and construction probe has its own argv, stdout, stderr, exit, limits, identity, timestamp, and classification receipt.
alternative_probe_contract.reachability_gate: The runner must execute the route's alternative probe even when the qualified probe exits nonzero, times out, is killed, or reports absence. A scheduler that suppresses the alternative makes the route UNKNOWN.
alternative_probe_contract.credit_gate: Alternative credit is route-local. A probe for one path, sibling, tag, wrapper, or ancestor cannot grant PARTIAL to another route.

state_effect.qualified_present_and_observables_equal: MATCH regardless of a related alternative, because the exact public obligation is satisfied.

math.required: For each route with a related bare or math-mode form, place that form in an independent source and process; never append it after repr(math.<member>) in the same evaluation.

html.invocation_template: html.elem("<tag>") with route-appropriate argument/content controls in a separate bilateral process
html.qualified_route_to_literal_tag_rule: Strip the exact html. prefix and pass the remaining route component as the literal tag. No shared html.elem("div") probe satisfies another route.
html.credit: A valid functional bilateral html.elem literal-tag result requires PARTIAL when the corresponding html.<tag> qualified route is absent.

instance_members.accepted_construction_shape: A minimal valid document plus public query/introspection/projection that yields the instance without evaluating the qualified ancestor constructor being classified.
instance_members.failure_policy: If no independent valid construction is demonstrated, classify UNKNOWN(UNSUPPORTED_CONSTRUCTION) or the more specific control failure; never ABSENT.

control_separation_r2.global_poisoning_forbidden: A control may block only routes whose declared observable depends on that control. HTML target or fixture failure cannot overwrite a completed non-HTML route result.

eval_target_flag.reason: The vanila CLI accepts eval --target; the crystalline CLI rejects it before the expression. Using it as a common prerequisite tests CLI asymmetry rather than the route.
eval_target_flag.gap_preservation: Record the asymmetric exit, stderr and argv as an out-of-denominator public CLI difference. Do not discard, normalize, or use it to classify any frozen route.

parser_and_feature_control.applies_to: All eval-based route probes, with the same feature set as the route profile.
parser_and_feature_control.purpose: Prove common eval CLI parsing, expression parsing, serialization, and feature-option parsing without selecting an asymmetric target.

required_public_projection: rendered text contains HTML target fixture
html_target_and_fixture_control.purpose: Prove feature activation, target selection and fixture/export path independently from any investigated HTML route.
html_target_and_fixture_control.failure_policy: Preserve the bilateral receipts and the target gap. Block only HTML-target-dependent routes as UNKNOWN with the exact phase reason; never call it PARSER_CONTROL_FAILED unless expression parsing actually failed.

html_api_valid_args_control.execution: Use a standalone compile --features html --format html fixture containing the minimal public call html.elem("div"); do not use eval --target.
html_api_valid_args_control.required_separation: Own process, argv, streams, exit, artifact and projection receipts; not concatenated after target or route probes.
html_api_valid_args_control.purpose: Separate validity of a known HTML API call from route-specific qualified and literal-tag probes.
html_api_valid_args_control.credit_boundary: This control proves only the common HTML API/argument fixture. It grants no existence or PARTIAL credit to any of the 44 route-specific tags.

html_route_execution.qualified_and_alternative_transport: For observations requiring target html, compile separate minimal fixtures with --features html --format html. Use eval only for target-independent qualified-access morphology and never pass --target.

execution_contract.processes: Use distinct processes for a route's qualified probe, every applicable alternative probe, and required instance-construction probe whenever an earlier diagnostic or abort could hide a later observation.
execution_contract.on_limit_or_truncation: UNKNOWN with a literal resource reason_code

parser, feature, target, fixture and API failures are attributed separately
no HTML-control failure contaminates non-HTML routes

owner_ledger_schema.ownership_policy: Read full candidate L0 only after route measurement; prove exact 1:1 productive consumer; never infer by name or directory.
owner_ledger_schema.unproved_owner_policy: Keep as nucleation debt; do not route directly to implementation.

backlog_schema.recommendation_policy: Exactly one smallest ABSENT, PARTIAL, or DIFFERENCE cause with unique current owner and complete witness; otherwise literal null plus blocking reason.

focal_gate: Validate both common eval parser/feature argv templates on both binaries for default and feature-bearing profiles.
Validate the compile-based target/fixture control bilaterally for html and html+a11y, with output projection and exact phase reason codes.
Run one HTML qualified route plus its literal-tag alternative and one non-HTML boundary route to prove applicability isolation.
Attack rejection of asymmetric eval --target, global poisoning, target failure mislabeled as parser failure, and per-product flag substitution.
Only after the focal vector passes, repeat the full discriminatory corpus direct, direct-repeat and reverse before a new preseal.

closure_criteria: Every one of the 93 exact routes has exactly one state.
Every state has current reproducible bilateral evidence and a proven owner or literal owner-absence reason.
All numeric decisions record HEAD, working tree, timestamp, argv, and product hashes.
The mutation score is exactly 1.0 and order invariance holds.
No L0, Nucleus, or L1-L4 byte changed.
The report makes exactly one qualified next-product-step recommendation or records why none is legally selectable.
claim_boundary: The verdict covers only executed public observables for the exact frozen denominator of 93 routes; it never establishes general functional parity of Typst.
